newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Fuel shortages threaten to paralyse Bulgaria.
newsitem.headline: Fuel shortages threaten to paralyse Bulgaria.

text.p: Fuel shortages threaten to paralyse Bulgaria as the country lacks cash for crude supplies but black market sales are flourishing.

"For the last one or two weeks the lack of diesel has been drastic and 18 transport firms in the country's biggest towns have reduced to the minimum the number of buses," deputy transport minister Vasil Rangelov told Reuters on Wednesday.
Petrol stations are often closed, and Rangelov said the national railway's diesel locomotives were about to stop due to the fuel shortages.
Rangelov said the new interim government, which was announced on Wednesday, was expected to release 200 tonnes of fuel from the state reserves.
State radio said Bulgarian fuel was still being smuggled to Macedonia, where prices are higher. Newspapers say a black market has sprung up inside Bulgaria.
Reductions in bus transport in the mining town of Pernik have caused problems for production, deputy mayor Malin Ivanov said by telephone.
"I can not guarantee the miners transportation to their working places but as far as I know not all of them are working as there is not enough diesel for their machines," Ivanov said.
The town of Vratsa in western Bulgaria is trying to avoid work stoppages in plants including the chemical firm Chimko.
"We are trying to arrange some fuel deliveries by private firms as otherwise tomorrow we will be forced to stop work in the industrial plants," said deputy mayor Vlado Dimitrov.

Bulgaria's biggest state-run refinery Neftochim, which supplies almost the whole domestic market, lacks cash to buy crude or settle its huge debts to suppliers, who are refusing crude deliveries to the plant in Bourgas.
As a result the refinery is distributing limited volumes of 680 tonnes of petrol and 680 tonnes of diesel per day, plant spokeswoman Tatyana Hadzhieva told Reuters.
Neftochim has been refining 8,500 tonnes of crude per day since Tuesday, while its daily capacity is 25,000, she added.
The refinery, which has in stock 45,000 tonnes of crude, needs credits to ensure its crude supplies until the end of the year, plant officials said.
A 66,300-tonne tanker from Russia's Rosbulneft arrived on Wednesday at the Bourgas port under its February contract for crude deliveries to Neftochim, transport officials said.
